inconsistencies: ArgsManager chain, order matters: #16545 -> #17580 -> {#17783, #17493 -> #17581}. #17783 scored near the top on its own but cannot be reviewed before its bases; start at #16545.

#31260 claims to be the foundation for runtime type checking in #16545, while #16545 claims to unblock #17580/#17783/#22978; these are overlapping settings-typing efforts by the same author and the intended merge order should be settled before either is reviewed deeply. #36295 is a small prerequisite cleanup that simplifies #31260.

Logging level/configuration work overlaps four ways: #34038 (replace -loglevel with -trace) and #35387 (make -loglevel work alone plus a loglevel RPC) solve the same operator pain point with different interfaces - pick one first, #34038 has the broader change. #35355 duplicates both #34038's -trace flag and #35322's atomic category bitmasks; #35322 should be reviewed first for the lock-free part. #34730 is explicitly gated on #34038.

#29256 is stacked on #34778, which carries an unwithdrawn Concept NACK; the logging-context chain cannot progress until that approach dispute is decided, so #34778 should be triaged first despite being the lesser change.
util::Result chain: #25665 is the prerequisite for #26022, #25722 and #29700; reviewing any dependent before #25665 wastes effort.

File I/O error handling overlaps: #36049 (don't terminate on buffered write failure), #36210 (include the OS error in AutoFile failures) and #35676 (abort with diagnostics in CheckDiskSpace/FlatFileSeq) all touch how storage failures surface. #36049 should be reviewed first; #35676's deliberate abort conflicts with #36049's goal of graceful shutdown, and reviewers have already disputed it on those grounds.
#36190 is a test for the behavior introduced by #36105 on Windows; it is only reviewable after that fix.
Both silent-payments PRs are blocked on the same upstream libsecp256k1 work (#1799) and #35302 additionally depends on #35301; #32966 (receiving) is the entry point.
#19460 depends on #10102 and #29409 and unblocks #19461; its utils content is only the -ipcconnect/-ipcbind plumbing.
result.notes: Several PRs here are filed under utils only because their shared-primitive contribution lands in util/crypto/args (silent payments, index parallelization, IPC wrapper); they are banded on that contribution plus the measurable effect, not on the feature as a whole. The top of the list was expanded into P1 because five PRs fix data loss, node crashes, a memory-safety bug and a platform regression, which is a different level of consequence from the refactor and logging work that filled the rest of the original P2 band.
